figures.description: Process of Compaction Applies when establishing fundamental weight-volume relationships for any soil or rock being evaluated for compaction. Dry unit weight (γd) is defined as the weight of solids divided by total volume, or equivalently total unit weight divided by (1 + w/100). Degree of saturation (S) is the percentage of void space filled with water; it increases as water content increases at constant dry unit weight. Compaction removes air voids; once air can no longer escape (high S), further compaction requires reducing water content. Phase diagrams on the compaction plane (γd vs. w) visualize the transitions during compaction and wetting.

figures.description: DEVELOPMENT OF EARTH PRESSURES AND LOADS Applies to all buried structures (retaining walls, basement walls, ground anchors) where earth pressure calculations are required. Earth pressures on buried structures depend on relative movement between the structure and the surrounding soil. At-rest condition (K0): no movement, equal pressures on both sides, soil not at failure. Active condition: structure moves away from soil; horizontal stress decreases, soil extends to shear failure.
